title: Receptionists and Information Clerks
description: Answer inquiries and provide information to the general public, customers, visitors, and other interested parties regarding activities conducted at establishment and location of departments, offices, and employees within the organization.

tasks.text: Transmit information or documents to customers, using computer, mail, or facsimile machine.
Process and prepare memos, correspondence, travel vouchers, or other documents.
Take orders for merchandise or materials and send them to the proper departments to be filled.
Operate telephone switchboard to answer, screen, or forward calls, providing information, taking messages, or scheduling appointments.
Schedule appointments and maintain and update appointment calendars.
Schedule space or equipment for special programs and prepare lists of participants.
Greet persons entering establishment, determine nature and purpose of visit, and direct or escort them to specific destinations.
Receive payment and record receipts for services.
Analyze data to determine answers to questions from customers or members of the public.
Calculate and quote rates for tours, stocks, insurance policies, or other products or services.

clusters.label: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

tasks.text: Hear and resolve complaints from customers or the public.
Provide information about establishment, such as location of departments or offices, employees within the organization, or services provided.

Perform administrative support tasks, such as proofreading, transcribing handwritten information, or operating calculators or computers to work with pay records, invoices, balance sheets, or other documents.
Collect, sort, distribute, or prepare mail, messages, or courier deliveries.
Keep a current record of staff members' whereabouts and availability.
Perform duties, such as taking care of plants or straightening magazines to maintain lobby or reception area.
Enroll individuals to participate in programs and notify them of their acceptance.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: 3M Post-it App, Google Docs, Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, IBM Notes, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Corel WordPerfect Office Suite, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Accounting software
skills.def: Software to enable business functions relating to accounting, such as recording transactions or managing budgets. Examples: Bookkeeping software, Intuit QuickBooks.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.
